newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GOLF-SJOLAND MOVES IN WITH RECORD 61.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SJOLAND MOVES IN WITH RECORD 61.

text.p: Swede Patrik Sjoland narrowly missed birdie putts on the last two holes to lose a chance of becoming the first European Tour player to break 60 in a full event in the second round of the Czech Open on Friday.

Sjoland's 10-under-par 61 smashed the Karlstein course record by three strokes and earned him a share of the lead with Spain's young Ryder Cup prospect Ignacio Garrido and another Spaniard, Miguel Jimenez.
Early evening thunderstorms halted play with 36 players left to complete their second rounds on Saturday morning before the halfway cut is made for the third round later in the day.
First-round leader Scott Henderson of Britain was nine under with three holes left, two shots off the lead, when play stopped.
Sjoland, 26, was only a stroke off the European Tour record for 18 holes as he joined Garrido and Jimenez on 11-under-par 131, two strokes ahead of the field.

The Swede also equalled the best score of the year, Englishman Jamie Spence shooting 61 but with preferred lies in the Cannes Open, as he picked up six birdies going out and four by the time he came to the eighth tee, his 17th hole.
Needing two more birdies for the first 59, a putt of 18 feet spun out of the cup on the eighth and he just missed the hole at the ninth, his last, from 15 feet.
Sjoland had switched to an old putter and needed only 25 putts in his round.

"I started thinking about the record after I birdied the fourth, my 13th hole," said Sjoland, who led last year's Italian Open with five holes left before settling for second. "But when I lipped out on the eighth I knew it wasn't to be."
Garrido continued his Valderrama bid with a 65, while Jimenez posted 64. Another Swede, Daniel Chopra, is in the clubhouse on 133 after 63.

Garrido, only six weeks after his maiden success in the German Open, is on the brink of qualification for a place on Seve Ballesteros's team against the United States next month, currently lying 10th in the Cup table.
"I'm definitely more confident since I won my first title," said Garrido, who boosted himself with a second place in last week's Scandinavian Masters.
"Before winning, my mind was keeping me behind because I used to wonder if I'd ever live with great players like Langer, Faldo and Rocca and now I feel I can beat them."
Garrido can now clinch his Cup place three weeks before the qualifying deadline but ninth-placed Costantino Rocca of Italy is almost certain to miss the cut by a stroke.
Rocca could also be passed by Ireland's Padraig Harrington who is six off the lead after a 68.
